name: Aninka
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Aninka/Ninka (Nigeria, Kainji area): only Blench 2006 subclassification comments found; no grammar or phonology located

sources.note: Consonant/vowel charts copied from Blench 2011; no tone or stress information; cites only Blench 2008, Blench 2011, Ethnologue, Glottolog.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-030: create [aqk] Aninka (submitter Luther Hon, SIL Nigeria; adopted 2021-01-15). 9 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic case only: 2017 SIL Nigeria survey, 336-item wordlist comparison giving 40-48% lexical similarity with Numana dialects (Numbu, Gbantu), 2008 RTT mean 85% (sd 16%), separate identity. Cites Hon et al. 2017 Executive Summary (SIL Nigeria Archives).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request 2018-090: Numana [nbr] / Ningye [nns] (Luther Hon, SIL Nigeria), including Hon et al. 2017 Executive Summary of a Sociolinguistic Survey of the Numana Dialects Cluster.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic; p. 7 refers to 'Michael J. R. etal 2008. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Numana, Numbu, Aninka, and Ningye of Kaduna State, Nigeria'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. Entry 346 'Ninka'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; entry gives Sanga (Kaduna State, Sanga LGA), <5000 speakers, Benue-Congo: Plateau: Ninzic, source Blench (2005).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. 2011 [Glottolog: 2006]. The Ninka language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 19 Oct 2011, i+20 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. (Glottolog ref 21286, wordlist)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 Phonology (p. 1) gives vowel and consonant charts with the caveat that the phonology 'is based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative'; the heading '3.3 Tones' (p. 1) has no text under it. The 705-item wordlist (pp. 3-20) is tone-marked (high/low/rising/falling diacritics, e.g. kúnkún 'tree', mkpàn/mkpán 'stone', árîŋ 'roots', àndǐs 'star'). Stress/accent never mentioned.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. Prospecting proto-Plateau. Draft circulated for comment, 92 pp. Cambridge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only. p. 14, section 3.3 Tones: 'The great majority of Plateau languages have three level tones and often phonemic glides.' p. 5: 'Many Plateau language have fearsomely complex phonology, both at the level of consonants and tone.' Ninka occurs only in classification/data-source tables. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. n.d. [c. 2003-2011]. The Nunku language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft, 24 pp. (sister Ninzic variety)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; '3.3 Tones' empty. p. 1: transcription follows Mada orthographic conventions 'with mid-tone marked with a macron' (implies a three-level tone transcription for the Ninzic wordlists).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. [chapter, pp. 3-44; Glottolog ref 586184, linked to Ninzic]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent overview of Plateau research status; would confirm whether any fuller Ninka/Aninka description has appeared since the 2011 wordlist. Probably on rogerblench.info (captcha-blocked to this client) or academia.edu (not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Hon, Luther, Fittokka Gobak, Iris Sacson, John Muniru, John Sacson, Julius Dabet & Yakubu Danladi. 2017. Executive Summary of a Sociolinguistic Survey of the Aninka of Kaduna State. SIL Nigeria Archives.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Basis of the 2020 ISO split; contains the 348-item Aninka wordlist used for lexical similarity. Sociolinguistic in scope; a stress statement is unlikely but it is the most recent primary data on the language.

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J., Katarína Hannelová, Ezekiel Rhila & Zachariah Yoder. 2008. Sociolinguistic Survey of the Numana, Numbu, Aninka, and Ningye of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Unpublished report, Jos: SIL Nigeria.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other first-hand work naming Aninka; SIL survey reports of this series usually contain wordlists and occasionally a phonological note. Possibly deposited in SIL Electronic Survey Reports / SIL Nigeria archive (sil.

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1983. Beiträge zur Kenntnis der Sprachen des Nigerianischen Plateaus. Glückstadt: J.J. Augustin.

sources.note: Standard older comparative-descriptive treatment of Plateau languages cited by Blench for the Numana/Ninzic group; may carry a general prosodic remark (tone) for the Numana cluster in which Ninka was then included. Not expected to name Ninka.
